title: Great Leadership Development Plans Share Four Ingredients
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article critiques leadership development plans that lean too heavily on assessment without enough emphasis on actual growth, and proposes four essential ingredients for a plan that genuinely moves the needle: targeted skills and behaviors, formative experiences, knowledge acquisition, and deliberate relationship-building. It notes that leaders consistently credit experiences — job rotations, board service, facilitating meetings, mediating conflict — as their biggest source of growth, more than training alone. The piece also distinguishes standard one-year plans from the two-year plans typically used in succession planning, where more investment and organization is required. It closes with a paraphrase of Antoine de Saint-Exupéry to frame development planning as enabling the future rather than predicting it.
points: Effective development plans combine four ingredients: targeted skills/behaviors, formative experiences, knowledge acquisition, and relationship-building.
Leaders consistently credit real experiences — job rotation, board service, facilitating meetings, mediating conflict — as their biggest source of growth.
Knowledge transfer is best delivered through self-paced formats or direct conversations with experts and mentors.
Succession-track leaders often need two-year plans with the same four ingredients organized across a longer horizon.
quotes: Many plans rely too heavily on assessment and not enough on skill and knowledge development.
Study after study reveals that leaders credit experiences over every other form for their biggest advancements in leadership development.
Great plans make room for introductions, conversations, and dialogues with people they don’t presently talk with but need to.
Leaders in a succession protocol typically need more time and investment to be ready for the next role.
Great Leadership Development Plans prepare leaders for a future they can’t yet see.
